# Robust White test with bootstrap and effect sizes

<small>Source: [`R/robust_implementations.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/R/robust_implementations.R) · Help: `?performWhiteTestRobust`</small>

Extends [`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) with optional bootstrap resampling, confidence
intervals, effect size reporting, and power analysis.

## Usage

```r
performWhiteTestRobust(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  method = c("standard", "reduced"),
  bootstrap = FALSE,
  B = 999,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  parallel = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   A fitted [stats::lm](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) object representing the mean specification
    to be diagnosed.

`data`
:   A [base::data.frame](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html) (or object coercible to one) containing the
    variables referenced by `model`. It must include the observations used to
    fit `model` and will be checked for missing values.
    When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used. It holds the
    terms of the model rather than its variables (`log(x)` rather than `x`), so
    a model that transforms a variable needs `data`, as does a
    model with an `offset()` term, and so may a fit whose `weights` or `offset`
    argument is a column of the data, which the model frame holds as
    `(weights)` or `(offset)`.

`method`
:   Character string selecting the auxiliary specification.
    "standard" retains squares and cross-products, while "reduced"
    excludes cross-products for high-dimensional designs.

`bootstrap`
:   Logical, compute bootstrap diagnostics for the
    statistic and p-value? The bootstrap is [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md), so on
    a fit returned by [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md) each replicate estimates the weights again,
    its default since 0.15.0. There is no argument to hold them fixed here;
    [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md) with `reestimate_weights = FALSE` does that.

`B`
:   Number of bootstrap replications when `bootstrap = TRUE`.
    Defaults to 999, at which a bootstrap p-value of the form
    `(1 + #) / (B + 1)` gives an exact test at the 5% and 1% levels; it was
    1000 before 0.15.0. The value is recorded in `robust_details$bootstrap$B`
    whether or not the bootstrap runs.

`ci_level`
:   Confidence level for reported intervals.

`parallel`
:   Logical, allow parallel bootstrap evaluation when the
    `parallel` package is available. A seeded call gives the same result
    each time; see *Parallel replicates* in [`bootstrapTestStatistic()`](rbootstrap_test_statistic.md).

## Value

An object of class `htest` augmented with a
`robust_details` list containing bootstrap, effect size, and power
information.

## Details

Provides enriched inference around the White test by combining bootstrap
resampling (Efron & Tibshirani, 1993) with asymptotic approximations. The
`robust_details` element summarises interval estimates, effect sizes, and power
calculations to aid decision-making.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

White, H. (1980). A heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix estimator
and a direct test for heteroscedasticity. *Econometrica, 48*(4), 817–838.

Efron, B., & Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). *An Introduction to the Bootstrap*.
Chapman & Hall.

## See also

[`performWhiteTest()`](performWhiteTest.md) for the base statistic and
[`performWhiteTestBootstrap()`](performWhiteTestBootstrap.md) for a lighter-weight resampling option.

## Examples

```r
data(mtcars)
mod <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
performWhiteTestRobust(mod, mtcars, bootstrap = TRUE, B = 200)
```
